questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the present continuous tense?
Which sentence is in the past continuous tense?
questions.explanation: 'were playing' = past continuous (ongoing action in past).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the future continuous tense?

options.a: I will be studying at 9pm tonight.

questions.explanation: 'will be studying' = future continuous (ongoing action in future).

questions.questionText: Identify the present perfect continuous sentence.

options.a: I have been waiting for two hours.
options.c: I am waiting for two hours.
options.d: I will wait for two hours.

questions.questionText: Maria says: 'I have been studying English for three years and I still feel like learning more.' Which tense is used?
questions.explanation: 'have been studying' = present perfect continuous (action started in past, still continuing).

questions.subtopic: Modal verb could past ability basic
questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'could' for past ability?

options.a: When I was young, I could run very fast.
options.b: I could to run very fast.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'might' correctly?
Which sentence uses 'must' for prohibition?
Which sentence uses 'would' for polite request?

options.a: Would you please open the window?

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'shall' formally?
Identify the sentence with a zero conditional.

options.a: When ice melts, it turns to water.
options.b: If it rains tomorrow, I will bring an umbrella.
options.c: If I had a car, I would drive to work.
options.d: If I had studied, I would have passed.

questions.explanation: Zero conditional: When/If + present simple, present simple (general fact).

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses the first conditional to describe a real future?

options.a: If it is sunny tomorrow, we will go to the beach.
options.b: If it were sunny, we would go to the beach.
options.c: If it had been sunny, we would have gone.
options.d: When it is sunny, we go to the beach.

questions.explanation: First conditional: If + present simple, will + base verb (real future).

questions.questionText: Which sentence describes an unreal or hypothetical present situation?

options.a: If I had wings, I would fly to you.
options.b: If I have wings, I will fly to you.
options.c: If I had wings, I would have flown to you.
options.d: If I had wings, I flew to you.

questions.explanation: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb (hypothetical).

questions.questionText: If you had superpowers for one day, what would you do? Identify the conditional type used.
questions.explanation: Second conditional: If + past simple, would + base verb = hypothetical/unreal.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'Someone will repair the road.'
questions.explanation: Passive future: will be + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They are building a new school.'

options.a: A new school is being built.
options.c: A new school was being built.

questions.explanation: Passive present continuous: is/are being + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'They were painting the house.'
questions.explanation: Passive past continuous: was/were being + past participle.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'The chef cooks the meal.'

options.a: The meal is cooked by the chef.
options.b: The meal is cooking by the chef.
options.c: The meal cooks by the chef.
options.d: The meal cooked by the chef.

questions.explanation: Passive present simple: am/is/are + past participle + by agent.

questions.questionText: Change to passive: 'Shakespeare wrote Hamlet.'
questions.explanation: Passive past simple: was/were + past participle + by agent.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'I work in a hospital,' she said.

options.a: She said that she worked in a hospital.
options.b: She said she works in a hospital.
options.c: She says she worked in a hospital.
options.d: She said I work in a hospital.

questions.explanation: Reported speech: present simple → past simple.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'Where do you live?' she asked.

options.b: She asked where do I live.
options.d: She asked where did I live.

questions.explanation: Reported question: statement form + tense backshift.

questions.questionText: Convert: 'Please sit down,' the teacher said.

options.a: The teacher asked me to sit down.
options.b: The teacher said please sit down.
options.c: The teacher said to sit down.
options.d: The teacher said that sit down.

questions.explanation: Reported command: asked/told + person + to + base verb.

questions.questionText: When converting to reported speech, 'today' usually becomes:
questions.explanation: Time/place words shift: today → that day, here → there, now → then.

questions.questionText: Identify the object pronoun.

options.a: I saw him at the park.
options.b: I saw he at the park.
options.c: I saw his at the park.
options.d: I saw himself at the park.

questions.questionText: Identify the reflexive pronoun.
Which sentence uses 'some' correctly?

options.a: There are some apples in the basket.
options.b: There are some apple in the basket.
options.c: There are any apples in the basket.
options.d: There is some apples in the basket.

questions.explanation: 'some' + plural countable noun in positive sentence.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'many' correctly?

options.a: There are many students in the hall.
options.b: There is many students in the hall.
options.c: There are much students in the hall.
options.d: There is much student in the hall.

questions.questionText: Which sentence uses 'little' correctly?

options.c: I have a little milks left.

questions.questionText: Which sentence correctly uses 'most' with the noun?
Identify the gerund as object.
questions.explanation: 'reading' = gerund (verb + ing) as object of verb 'enjoy'.

questions.questionText: Choose the synonym of 'rapid'.
Choose the antonym of 'generous'.
What does 'to bite off more than you can chew' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Bite off more than you can chew' = take on more than you can handle.

questions.questionText: What does the idiom 'it's bucketing down' mean?
What does 'once in a blue moon' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Once in a blue moon' = very rarely.

questions.questionText: What does 'to feel under the weather' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Feel under the weather' = feeling slightly ill.

questions.questionText: What does 'get along' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Get along' = have a good relationship with someone.

questions.questionText: What does 'give in' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Give in' = surrender or yield to pressure.

questions.questionText: What does 'keep on' mean?
What does 'look up' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Look up' = search for information (in a book or online).

questions.questionText: What does 'pick up' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Pick up' = lift, collect, or learn (multiple meanings).

questions.questionText: What does 'put away' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Put away' = store something in its proper place.

questions.questionText: Which is the correct collocation with 'make'?
Which is the correct collocation with 'have'?
Identify the word family.
Read: 'Anna has three cats. They are black and white. Their names are Mimi, Lili, and Lili.' How many cats does Anna have?
Read: 'Tom's face turned red. He looked away quickly.' How did Tom feel?
Read: 'Please remember to bring your passport and visa to the airport.' What is the purpose?
Read: 'I believe that every student should have access to free education.' What is the speaker's attitude?
Read: 'Pollution is a serious problem. Many cities have dirty air. This causes health issues. We must act now.' What is the main idea?

options.a: Pollution is serious and needs action.

questions.explanation: Main idea: pollution is serious + need for action.

questions.questionText: Read: 'Dolphins are mammals. They breathe air and feed their young with milk. They live in the ocean.' Which detail supports that dolphins are mammals?

options.a: They feed their young with milk.

questions.explanation: Supporting detail: 'feed young with milk' = mammal characteristic.

questions.questionText: Read: 'First, we arrived at the airport. Then, we checked in our bags. Next, we went through security. Finally, we boarded the plane.' What happened first?
Read: 'It rained heavily, so the match was cancelled.' What is the effect?
Read: 'Unlike a bicycle, which has two wheels, a tricycle has three wheels.' What is the difference?
questions.explanation: Comparison: bicycle (2 wheels) vs tricycle (3 wheels).

questions.questionText: Read: 'The arid desert has no water and few plants.' What does 'arid' mean?
Read: 'Lily always shares her toys with her friends. She listens when others talk.' What kind of person is Lily?
Read: 'Online learning has become popular. Many students study from home using laptops. This saves travel time. However, some students miss classroom interaction.' What is the topic sentence?

options.b: Many students study from home using laptops.

questions.explanation: Topic sentence: 'Online learning has become popular' (general statement).

questions.questionText: Read: 'While the city is busy and crowded, the countryside is quiet and peaceful.' What is the contrast?
Read: 'GRAND SALE! 50% off all items. Limited time only. Visit us at Main Street.' What is this?
Read: 'NOTICE: Library closed for maintenance on Sunday, March 10. We apologize for the inconvenience.' What is this?
Which sentence is a simple sentence with one independent clause?

options.a: My cat sleeps on the couch.
options.b: My cat sleeps and the dog barks.
options.c: My cat sleeps when it is tired.
options.d: Although my cat is young, she sleeps a lot.

questions.explanation: Simple = one independent clause, no conjunction.

questions.questionText: Which is a compound sentence using 'and'?

options.a: I read the book and she watched a movie.
options.b: I read the book because she watched a movie.
options.c: When I read the book, she watched a movie.
options.d: I read the book while she watched.

questions.explanation: Compound: two independent clauses joined by 'and'.

questions.questionText: Which is a complex sentence with a 'because' clause?

options.a: I brought an umbrella because it looked like rain.
options.b: I brought an umbrella and it looked like rain.
options.c: I brought an umbrella while it rained.
options.d: I brought an umbrella; it rained.

questions.questionText: Which is a compound-complex sentence?

options.a: Although it rained, we stayed home and played games.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'She is tired. She keeps working.'

options.c: She is tired but working keeps.

questions.questionText: Choose the correct form: 'She ___ to school every day.'
Choose the correct article: '___ apple a day keeps the doctor away.'
Choose the correct preposition: 'She is good ___ Mathematics.'
Transform: 'They built the bridge.' to passive.

options.a: The bridge was built by them.
options.b: The bridge is built by them.
options.d: The bridge was build by them.

questions.explanation: Passive past: was + past participle + by agent.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'She read. He slept.' (use 'while')
Combine: 'The phone rang. I was sleeping.' (use 'when')

options.a: When the phone rang, I was sleeping.
options.b: The phone rang and I was sleeping.
options.c: The phone rang but I was sleeping.
options.d: While the phone rang, I was sleeping.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'Study hard. You will pass.' (use 'if')

options.a: If you study hard, you will pass.
options.b: Study hard and you will pass.
options.c: Study hard but you will pass.
options.d: Study hard or you will pass.

questions.questionText: Combine: 'It rained. We stayed home.' (use 'so')

options.a: It rained, so we stayed home.
options.b: It rained and we stayed home.
options.c: It rained but we stayed home.
options.d: It rained or we stayed home.

questions.questionText: Identify the error: 'She go to school every day.'
Identify the error: 'Yesterday I go to the park and played.'
Choose the appropriate formal email opening.
Choose the appropriate formal email closing for an unknown recipient.
Choose the polite request sentence.

options.a: I would appreciate it if you could send me the details.

questions.explanation: 'I would appreciate it if you could...' = polite formal request.

questions.questionText: What are the key details in a notice?
What is essential in a brief message?
questions.explanation: Brief message essentials: sender, recipient, key info.

questions.questionText: Choose the formal acceptance.

options.a: Thank you for the invitation. I would be delighted to attend.

questions.explanation: Formal acceptance: 'Thank you' + 'would be delighted to attend'.

questions.questionText: Choose the formal apology for a serious mistake.

options.a: I sincerely apologize for the inconvenience and will ensure it does not happen again.

questions.explanation: Formal apology: 'I sincerely apologize' + corrective action.

questions.questionText: Choose the formal thank you note.

options.a: I would like to express my sincere gratitude for your assistance.

questions.explanation: Formal thank you: 'I would like to express my sincere gratitude'.

questions.questionText: Choose the polite email request.

options.a: Would you mind sending me the file at your earliest convenience?

questions.questionText: Choose the most formal way to express a complaint about a product.

options.a: I wish to lodge a formal complaint regarding the defective product.

questions.explanation: Formal complaint: 'I wish to lodge a formal complaint'.

questions.questionText: How would you ask to see a doctor?

options.a: I'd like to make an appointment to see Doctor Lim, please.

questions.explanation: Doctor: 'I'd like to make an appointment to see Doctor Lim.'

questions.questionText: How would you book a restaurant table?

options.a: I'd like to reserve a table for four at 7pm, please.

questions.explanation: Restaurant: 'reserve a table' + party size + time.

questions.questionText: How would you ask about train times?

options.a: Excuse me, when does the next train to Kuala Lumpur leave?

questions.explanation: Train: 'when does the next train leave' = asking schedule.

questions.questionText: How would you ask about parcel rates?

options.a: Could you tell me the postage rate for this parcel to Japan?

questions.explanation: Post office: 'postage rate' = asking cost of mailing.

questions.questionText: How would you ask to borrow a book?

options.a: Excuse me, may I borrow this book for two weeks?

questions.explanation: Library: 'may I borrow this book for two weeks' = polite request.

questions.questionText: How would you introduce yourself at a parent-teacher meeting?

options.a: Hello, I'm Mrs. Lee, Tom's mother. Thank you for meeting with me.

questions.questionText: How would you wish someone a happy birthday?

options.a: Happy birthday! Wishing you all the best.

questions.explanation: Birthday: 'Happy birthday! Wishing you all the best.'

questions.questionText: How would you start a conversation about weather?
questions.explanation: Weather conversation: 'Lovely day, isn't it?' = small talk.

questions.questionText: How would you ask for a different size?

options.a: Excuse me, do you have this in a larger size?

questions.explanation: Shopping: 'do you have this in a larger size' = polite.

questions.questionText: How would you ask for directions to a hospital?

options.a: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the nearest hospital?

questions.explanation: Directions: 'could you tell me how to get to' = polite request.

questions.questionText: Read: 'The moon is bright / Up in the sky / Stars twinkle at night / As time goes by.' What is the rhyme scheme?
Read: 'I wandered lonely as a cloud / That floats on high o'er vales and hills' Who is the speaker?
Read: 'The trees sway gently in the breeze / The birds sing sweetly in the trees.' What is the theme?
Read: 'The moon hung low, the stars shone bright / A peaceful calm filled the night.' What is the mood?
Read: 'Her smile is sunshine.' What figurative language is used?
questions.explanation: 'Her smile IS sunshine' = direct comparison = metaphor.
